method: Independent source tracing, intercepted synthetic-data execution, native Rizin disassembly; no live external requests or native specimen execution.

samples.marker_line: Aokigahara reconstruction: AI credential export; add GCM encryption
samples.identification: Functional Go reconstruction of Aokigahara AI-agent credential collector; not an original recovered malware binary.
execution_trace: Collect requires caller-provided root, destination, receiver public key, gate token and session. There is no entry point or automatic activation.
It reads 13 targeted Claude/Codex/Copilot/Kiro/Gemini/Codeium/Cursor/Windsurf auth/configuration paths under that root, skipping unavailable files and adding original contents to a ZIP.

It generates ephemeral X25519 material, derives the symmetric key from the shared secret via SHA-256, submits the public key to /gate/handshake, encrypts the ZIP using AES-GCM with a 12-byte nonce, POSTs nonce+ciphertext to /gate/chunk and signals /gate/complete.

A custom in-process RoundTripper intercepted all requests. With one synthetic Codex auth file, server-side key derivation and GCM decryption recovered that exact file from the ZIP. No socket or external HTTP request was made.
samples.judgment: The only implemented collection workflow targets reusable cross-vendor authentication stores and exports their contents in an encrypted receiver-readable archive. That functional credential-stealer behavior tips the verdict even though this source was reconstructed for research.
samples.missing_context: No original campaign binary, caller, actual root, receiver or execution authorization is supplied. Do not infer deployment or precise KDF compatibility with original malware.
samples.changes: Retain all four hostile findings; add a notable Seal-operation rule bound to a Go GCM constructor.

samples.marker_line: i5149 probe: disclosed host report; correct OOB callback severity
samples.identification: i5149 authorized-pentest probe packaged as i88-probe-node; setup.py version 0.2.0, project metadata version 0.1.0.
execution_trace: All six original ZIP entries match the provided extracted files byte-for-byte.

setup.py performs an immediate JSON POST before setuptools.setup, reporting marker, hostname, numeric UID, username, working directory, Python version, up to 50 environment-variable names and up to six arguments.
install.py performs a similar immediate POST with up to 40 environment-variable names. It does not serialize environment values.
__init__.py defines a trivial ComfyUI-style node returning (1,); i5149_probe.py contains a constant. No secret-store reads, payload activation or persistence are present in the complete archive.

Both reporting modules were executed with urlopen intercepted and deterministic synthetic host/user/environment queries. Exactly two POSTs were recorded and a sentinel environment value never appeared in either body.
samples.judgment: Explicit testing disclosure in source and project description is consistent with the bounded execution-context probe. That purpose, complete transparent source and absence of additional hostile functionality tip the balance toward BENIGN. The disclosure is not treated as proof of deployment authorization or as a rule exemption.
samples.missing_context: Publisher ownership of the collector and authorization on a particular machine remain unverified. Host, cwd and argv reporting is privacy-relevant and still merits the accurate suspicious finding.
samples.changes: Correct the generic hostile callback co-occurrence rule to a notable HTTP request/beacon observation; retain both members' suspicious bound host-identity-body findings.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Raw ML probability falls from 0.9976356 to 0.9734319; the calibrated level stays -1 before and after. The original queue HOSTILE prior is not corroborated by independent code review. Current rule output remains suspicious, which is compatible with a benign testing tool.

samples.marker_line: Winlogon DDoS bot: remote execution and floods; retain persistence
samples.identification: Native Winlogon DDoS/download bot posing as Get MAC Address / Server.exe. Collection filename family labels are not attribution evidence.
execution_trace: main at 0x402120 builds Windows/Tasks/conime.exe, invokes 0x401f80 to append it to Winlogon Userinit, copies and launches itself hidden, and reaches a self-delete setup for the prior image.
0x401f80 constructs normal system Userinit plus comma plus installed image and writes the REG_SZ through the dynamically resolved RegSetValueExA pointer at 0x407c20.
0x401dd0 transforms controller bytes as ((byte - 44) & 255) XOR 44; independent decoding yields www.asis0day.biz:8095. 0x4015f0 splits host/port and connects.
0x401910 sends a machine profile assembled at 0x402350, receives a length/task header through the recv helper at 0x4017d0, reads the body and selects handlers.
The download handler at 0x401c58 resolves URLDownloadToFileA, consumes the received URL and passes the same temporary destination pathname to WinExec at 0x401c92.
The task-selected flood dispatcher at 0x401030 starts worker threads. At 0x402a40 a worker sends 18 datagrams per burst, waits 20 ms, and repeats until the shared stop flag changes.

Additional HTTP workers generate randomized .asp/.html/.htm request paths through templates referenced at 0x4034fc, 0x403776 and 0x4039f0. The assembled request reaches repeated send calls at 0x403f76 under the same stop flag.
samples.judgment: Reusable remote tasking, unsolicited download-and-run, attack floods, disguised self-installation and unwanted login activation contradict the claimed MAC-address utility purpose.
samples.missing_context: No live controller reachability, installed victim host or final downloaded executable was observed. None is needed to establish these hostile paths.
samples.changes: Move the unchanged notable Userinit-write atom into micro-behaviors/os/registry/write and update its hostile composite plus existing verification script. All six hostile findings are retained.

limitations: Installed Atomscan embeds an older validator without the documented metadata/file/naming 101-rule budget. Before/after scans consistently use CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0, --no-update, --mode slow and --follow=none; final repository validation uses the newer source-tree Cleave release with full checks.
Installed Atomscan reports model feature spec v18 against extractor v19 and flow limitations. Model probability, calibration level and parser gaps are preserved rather than treated as proof.
Triage and the referenced Check Point article were inaccessible through the web tool. Findings rely on supplied bytes and traced effects, not external claims or collector filenames.
No fetched dependency caused a finding. The Python archive declares no external runtime dependency and no dependency exception was added.
material_detection_losses: No supported attack behavior was lost. Only the unsupported hostile inference from generic quiet OOB co-occurrence was removed; its observable evidence remains notable. Userinit changes are placement-only and all existing hostile findings on both malicious samples remain.
